title: Corpse Reviver No. 2
description: Equal parts gin, Cocchi, orange liqueur and lemon; absinthe-misted coupe.
beforeYouStart: Load the atomiser with absinthe. No atomiser? Swirl a few drops in the cold glass and tip out the excess.

steps.do: Add everything except the absinthe to the shaker tin.
Fill with ice and shake hard.
Mist the chilled coupe with absinthe, so it scents the drink without taking over.
Double strain into the glass through the Hawthorne and a fine strainer.
Fold the twist over the surface to spray its oils, then drop it in.

items: Craddock's original called for Kina Lillet, which is no longer made. It carried more quinine bite, so Cocchi Americano is the closer match.
With Lillet Blanc or another white vermouth, pick one with noticeable bitterness, or add a dash of orange bitters to make up for it.
The book gives 20 ml (2/3 oz) of each. Scaled to 3/4 oz to land on a standard jigger line; keep all four equal and the drink is unchanged.

source.name: Harry Craddock's recipe, from Strong, Sweet and Bitter: Your Guide to All Things Cocktails, Bartending and Booze from Behind the Bar by Cara Devine, p. 119
